context_only: ## 2. Prior art and the lessons taken

tasks.title: Add the seven run workflow fields
tasks.acceptance:
model.Workflow gains run_max_units, run_max_wall_clock_seconds, run_max_budget_usd, run_max_unit_budget_usd, run_max_unit_retries, runner and notify_cmd with the documented defaults and ranges.
Each numeric field accepts both range endpoints and rejects one step outside; notify_cmd resolves from .tp/local.json only.
tp config --resolved, tp config --extract and tp validate --project cover all seven (test 16, 69).
tasks.closed_reason:
- model.Workflow now carries §7's seven run fields with the documented defaults — run_max_units 100, run_max_wall_clock_seconds 28800, both budgets 0 (disabled / flag omitted) as decimal dollars, run_max_unit_retries 1, runner "claude" as raw JSON so the resolver (not this layer) tells its three shapes apart, and notify_cmd; the six layerable ones are presence-tracked in WorkflowOverride and resolve through the existing task-override > project-config > built-in path, verified by tests asserting each default and each layer winning per field, including an explicit 0 retries beating a project value.
- Every numeric range is enforced at the same read-time clamp the existing fields use: an out-of-range value is dropped to absent with a warning and resolves to the built-in default. A table test drives each of the five fields through a real .tp/config.json and asserts BOTH endpoints are accepted (1/10000, 60/604800, 0/5, 0/10000, 0/1000) and that one step outside each — one unit for the integers, one cent for the budgets — is rejected, so an inclusive bound cannot pass as exclusive.
- notify_cmd resolves from .tp/local.json only: it is a LocalConfig key, is deliberately absent from knownWorkflowKeys (so a workflow block carrying it reports "unknown workflow key"), and is never hoisted by --extract or compared by --project. Verified by a test where config.json and local.json both name one and the local value wins with the unknown-key warning raised.
- All three config surfaces cover the seven: tp config --resolved reports each with its layer (override/project/default, and local/default for notify_cmd), tp config --extract hoists the six unanimous ones and never notify_cmd, and tp validate --project reports run-field deviations with budgets printed as decimal dollars and runner compared as raw JSON. Dogfooded with the freshly built binary on tp's own repo (all seven report default, runner "claude") and on a scratch project where a per-kind runner map, a local notify_cmd and an out-of-range run_max_units each reported as documented.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... , golangci-lint run, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh all exit 0.

Out of scope: tp set --workflow (and --project) still rejects the five numeric run fields as unknown workflow fields, so they are authorable only by hand-editing .tp/config.json or a task file's workflow block; §5.1's "tp set --workflow run_max_*= above the resolved value" fence assumes that setter exists, so the unattended-fence or run-command task needs it added to editableWorkflowFields/workflowFieldRange with float support for the two budgets.

tasks.title: Resolve the runner field's three shapes
tasks.acceptance:
runner resolves as a template name, a runner object, or a per-kind map with default; an object carrying cmd is a runner and anything else is a map.
A map without default and a runner object without cmd are both usage errors (test 56).

tasks.title: Ship both built-in runner templates
tasks.acceptance:
The claude template resolves to its documented argv including --permission-mode auto, appending --max-budget-usd only when run_max_unit_budget_usd is non-zero; opencode resolves to run with the prompt.
Every placeholder resolves, and an unresolved one is a usage error raised before any child is spawned (test 10).

tasks.title: Add the TP_RUNNER_SEAM test seam
tasks.acceptance:
TP_RUNNER_SEAM resolves to a runner whose args are the documented positional list and whose spend_key is total_cost_usd, outranking every layer including CLI.
The fake runner records each invocation's argv, environment, spawn time and exit time (test 1).

tasks.title: Read spend from the runner log
tasks.acceptance:
After a child exits the driver reads total_cost_usd for claude or the declared spend_key, and reports spend null for a runner declaring none.
A runner with no spend_key leaves cap-budget inert and is reported once at run start; a per-kind map names its unmetered kinds (tests 11, 66).

tasks.title: Define the eight unit kinds
tasks.acceptance:
An eight-kind enum carries each kind's durable-write predicate and concurrency from the table.
Each predicate is decidable from the artifacts it names with no baseline, and the role predicate ignores blank and whitespace-only lines (tests 18, 48, 59).
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/unitkind.go defines UnitKind as §3.3's eight kinds in table order (implement, review-role, review-record, review-resolve, decompose, audit-role, audit-record, audit-fix), each carrying its concurrency (Concurrency()/Concurrent(): only the two role kinds are ConcurrencySiblingRoles, every other kind and any unknown value is alone) and its durable-write predicate (DurableWrite(UnitTarget)); verified by table tests over all eight kinds asserting the enum, the order, the defensive copy, ParseUnitKind's rejection of near-misses, and each kind's concurrency value.
- Every predicate is decidable from the artifacts §3.3 names for it with no baseline: TestUnitKind_DurableWrite_DecidableWithNoBaseline runs each kind in a fresh temp dir where the artifacts are written before the predicate is ever called (so no 'before' observation exists), asserts a repeat call answers identically (state, not delta), and pairs each with a one-artifact-short case plus a nothing-written case; the audit-fix case passes on a row disposed with no code change at all (test 18), and an unknown kind is never complete.
- The role predicate reads content lines only: TestUnitKind_RolePredicate_ContentLinesOnly runs both role kinds over a trailing newline, a file of blank and whitespace-only lines, an empty file, an unparseable line, a truncated row, a non-object line, and a missing file (tests 48, 59), with the .part-only case failing because the rename that completes the write never happened.
- Gate green on the committed tree: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0.
Out of scope: the recorded round-file name format (review-round-<N>.ndjson / audit-round-<N>.ndjson) is now spelled in three places — internal/cli/review_record.go, internal/cli/audit_record.go and engine.roundFilePath — so the two writers and this reader can drift; centralizing it belongs to whichever later task next touches the record paths.

tasks.title: Map each unit kind to its brief command
tasks.acceptance:
Each kind resolves to the documented brief_command, with the record kinds' merge step skipped when merged.ndjson already exists.
A unit succeeded when it exited 0 and its durable write is present; either alone is a failed attempt (tests 51, 57).
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/briefcommand.go maps every §3.3.1 unit kind to the brief_command the oracle supplies: tp next --brief (implement), tp review/tp audit <spec> (the role kinds), tp review/tp audit <spec> --status (review-resolve / audit-fix), tp resume (decompose), and the two-step record brief '[ -f $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson ] || tp <phase> --merge $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-*.ndjson -o $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson; tp <phase> <spec> --record $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson' for review-record and audit-record, with an unknown kind returning "" the way DurableWrite returns false; verified by a table pinning all eight strings byte for byte against the spec text, and by running each record brief through /bin/sh with a fake tp on PATH — the merge step is invoked when merged.ndjson is absent and skipped when it is present, so a re-run never merges over the dispositions §6.3 accumulates (test 57).
- UnitKind.Succeeded(exitCode, target) is the driver's whole success test — exit 0 AND the kind's durable write present — verified over the four combinations: only exit 0 with the write present succeeds, and both an exit 0 with nothing written and a non-zero exit over a complete write are failed attempts (test 51).
- Gate green before closing: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0 issues, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0.

tasks.title: Export the child environment variables
tasks.acceptance:
Every child receives TP_RUN_ID as a ULID, TP_RUN_DIR absolute, TP_ROUND_DIR derived from phase and round, TP_FILE, TP_UNIT_ID, TP_UNIT_KIND, TP_UNIT_SEQ and TP_PHASE.
TP_ROUND and TP_ROUND_DIR are unset, not empty, outside a round-based phase, and driver variables are applied after the runner.env merge (tests 20, 37, 46).
source_sections: #### 3.1.1 Units, ids and the child environment
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/childenv.go builds every child's environment from §3.1.1: ChildEnv merges runner.env over the parent and then applies the driver's own variables last (TP_RUN_ID, TP_RUN_DIR, TP_FILE, TP_UNIT_ID, TP_UNIT_KIND, TP_UNIT_SEQ, TP_PHASE, TP_ROUND, TP_ROUND_DIR and §5.1's TP_UNATTENDED=1); NewULID emits the canonical 26-character Crockford ULID for TP_RUN_ID, RunDir resolves the absolute .tp/runs/<run-id>, RunBase strips the .tasks.json suffix for the run artifacts' <base>, and RoundDir derives .tp/rounds/<base>/<phase>-r<round>. Verified by tests asserting every variable's documented form, TP_RUN_DIR absolute, the round directory keyed by base+phase+round, and the ULID's alphabet, length, uniqueness over 200 draws and decoded timestamp.
- TP_ROUND and TP_ROUND_DIR are removed rather than emptied when the oracle reports round null, even when the parent environment or runner.env carried them (test 46), and driver variables outrank runner.env so an entry for TP_UNATTENDED, TP_RUN_ID, TP_ROUND_DIR or TP_UNIT_KIND never reaches the child while non-driver entries still extend and override the parent (test 20). Gate green: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0.
Out of scope: nothing found.

tasks.title: Take a run-scoped lock
tasks.acceptance:
tp run takes .tp/locks/run-<base>.lock for the whole run and never holds the task-file write lock while a child is in flight.
A child's own tp write succeeds during the run and a second tp run exits 4 (test 9).
source_sections: #### 3.1.1 Units, ids and the child environment

tasks.title: Add next_units to the resume oracle
tasks.acceptance:
tp resume --json gains next_units carrying {kind, id, brief_command} plus round, and next_action renders next_units[0].
A non-concurrent kind is never returned alongside another unit, and every assertion pinning resume's exact object set moves with the field (test 38).

tasks.title: Omit roles already satisfying the predicate
tasks.acceptance:
In a round-based phase next_units omits every role whose findings file satisfies the role predicate, and a malformed file is re-run rather than skipped.
After a round is recorded the oracle returns one audit-fix unit at a time and one review-resolve unit while a finding lacks a disposition (tests 45, 52).

tasks.title: Store last_failure outside the run state
tasks.acceptance:
A non-zero unit exit writes .tp/last_failure-<base>.json with the documented fields and a tp-authored summary, cleared only on the next success of the same (kind, id).
tp resume and tp brief surface it and it survives into the next run (test 23).

tasks.title: Record a gate failure from tp done
tasks.acceptance:
tp done writes last_failure with the gate's own output when its gate fails and TP_UNIT_KIND is set.
It writes nothing when that variable is absent, leaving the shipped command unchanged outside a run (test 61).

tasks.title: Write the run state file
tasks.acceptance:
.tp/run-<base>.json holds run_id, started_at, phase, stop_reason, totals and one row per unit attempt, written atomically.
A row is appended with null exit_code before its child spawns and updated after it exits, and totals restart at zero on a new run (test 12).
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/runstate.go writes §3.5's run state at .tp/run-<base>.json (RunStatePath, named per task file off RunBase and absolute like TP_RUN_DIR): RunState carries run_id, started_at, phase, stop_reason, totals {units, wall_clock_seconds, spend_usd} and one RunUnitRow per unit attempt {seq, kind, id, attempt, exit_code, duration_seconds, spend_usd, log_path}; every mutation rewrites the whole file through a unique temp file + rename, serialized by the recorder's mutex because concurrent role siblings finish in the same iteration and readers take no lock. Verified by tests asserting the documented top-level shape and the path form, and by eight concurrent siblings under -race with a lock-free reader beside them: every row survives, the file always parses and no .tmp is left behind.
- RunRecorder.StartUnit appends the row before the child is spawned with exit_code, duration_seconds and spend_usd forced to null (cleared from a copy, so the caller's value is untouched), and FinishUnit updates that row in place by seq — a seq no row carries is an error rather than an invented row. Totals are recomputed from the rows on every write, so units counts attempts (a retry is a second row) and spend sums only the metered ones, an unmetered unit staying null and accruing nothing. NewRunRecorder replaces any file a dead run left at the path, so units, spend, wall clock and stop_reason all restart at zero on a new run — caps bound a run, not a cycle. Verified by test 12's before/after assertions read from the raw JSON (null vs 0 is the distinction the two-write protocol rests on), an attempts test that agrees with Snapshot's accrual, and a second-run test asserting zeroed totals, no inherited rows and a fresh run_id.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... (0), golangci-lint run (0 issues), ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh (0).
Out of scope: the run state is not yet reachable from any command — ReadRunState and Snapshot exist for the run-status and cap tasks that own those surfaces, and the .tp/.gitignore entry for run-<base>.json belongs to gitignore-entries.

tasks.title: Own each unit's log file
tasks.acceptance:
A template omitting {log_path} has its child's stdout and stderr redirected to $TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl; one using the placeholder owns the file and is not redirected.
Every child is spawned with stdin closed so a runner reading stdin sees EOF (tests 60, 62).

tasks.title: Execute the driver loop
tasks.acceptance:
tp run [spec] reads cycle state, takes next_units, spawns concurrent kinds together and every other kind alone, re-reads state from disk, and checks caps.
The loop advances through implement, review and audit and stops with converged when the oracle reports phase release; a crashed driver resumes at the same unit (tests 2, 5, 6).

tasks.title: Attempt a unit its budgeted number of times
tasks.acceptance:
A unit is attempted 1 + run_max_unit_retries times, each attempt taking a fresh seq and log path.
The driver deletes a role unit's findings file and any stale .part immediately before spawning it, so a leftover cannot satisfy the retry's predicate (tests 8, 17, 65).

tasks.title: Record the nine stop reasons
tasks.acceptance:
Each of the nine stop_reason values is produced by its documented cause, and run_max_units, totals.units and units-done all count attempts.
No stop reason records a round, marks a phase converged, or closes a task its own unit did not close (tests 3, 4, 7, 33).

tasks.title: Order simultaneously satisfied stop reasons
tasks.acceptance:
When one checkpoint satisfies several rows the recorded reason is the documented first, with converged leading.
Two simultaneously satisfied conditions record the higher-precedence reason (test 34).

tasks.title: Evaluate caps between iterations only
tasks.acceptance:
Caps are checked between iterations, in-flight children run to completion and the driver kills nothing.
SIGINT and SIGTERM stop the run with interrupted, letting children finish and spawning no new unit (tests 41, 63).

tasks.title: Stop on a driver-side fatal error
tasks.acceptance:
A runner that cannot be exec'd, or a run directory that cannot be written, stops the run with driver-error and exit 4.
No unit is charged a failed attempt for it (test 70).

tasks.title: Pin tp run's exit codes
tasks.acceptance: tp run exits 0 on converged and 4 on every other stop_reason, and 2 on a usage error before the loop starts (test 54).

tasks.title: Report the run with tp run --status
tasks.acceptance:
tp run --status prints phase, units done, spend against each cap, the last unit's exit code and log path, stop_reason, and run_state as in_flight, crashed or stopped using the run lock.
It carries the divergence signals on an audit-phase stop, exits 0 when it can report and 3 when no run state exists, and takes no lock (tests 14, 35, 58).

tasks.title: List the next units with --dry-run
tasks.acceptance: tp run --dry-run prints the units the driver would execute next, exits 0, spawns nothing, writes no run state and takes no lock (tests 13, 58).

tasks.title: Strip the run surface under --compact
tasks.acceptance: Under --compact the run surface keeps stop_reason and the cap totals and strips per-unit rows and log paths (test 68).

tasks.title: Git-ignore the run artifacts
tasks.acceptance: The shipped .tp/.gitignore covers .tp/run-<base>.json, .tp/runs/, .tp/rounds/ and .tp/last_failure-<base>.json, and the fixture gains four entries (test 15).

tasks.title: Refuse user-only decisions when unattended
tasks.acceptance:
Under TP_UNATTENDED each of the four user-only operations exits 2 with its hint and exits 0 without the variable; a cap set to an equal or lower non-zero value exits 0, and a budget field set to 0 while a non-zero value resolves exits 2.
The env layer is ignored for every fenced field, runner and notify_cmd cannot be set at any layer, and the mode activates on any present non-empty value other than 0 (tests 19, 40, 64).

tasks.title: Add the tp escalate command
tasks.acceptance:
tp escalate writes $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json with the documented fields and one of the five decision values, and exits 2.
Two concurrent siblings each write their own, and outside a run it is a usage error (test 22).

tasks.title: Stop the run on an escalation record
tasks.acceptance:
A unit that wrote a valid escalation record stops the run with escalation whatever the harness exited with, is not counted as a failed attempt and sets no last_failure.
A record that fails schema validation, or an exit 2 with none, is judged as an ordinary attempt (tests 21, 47).

tasks.title: Invoke notify_cmd on a non-converged stop
tasks.acceptance:
notify_cmd fires on every non-converged stop, exec'd without a shell and split on whitespace, carrying TP_STOP_REASON, TP_RUN_ID and on an escalation TP_ESCALATION_PATH.
Its own failure is reported and never changes stop_reason (test 42).

tasks.title: Add tp audit --resolve
tasks.acceptance:
tp audit --resolve and --resolve-all dispose audit rows with the same dispositions and flags as their review counterparts and additionally accept a role:item_id selector.
An audit-fix unit that disposes its row without a code change satisfies its predicate (test 53).

tasks.title: Emit the round-scoped findings path
tasks.acceptance:
Under TP_ROUND_DIR, tp review and tp audit emit $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-<role>.ndjson.part per role as that role's output file, and the emitted filename is unchanged outside a run.
The record units merge $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-*.ndjson and write merged.ndjson only when absent, so a re-run preserves accumulated dispositions (tests 27, 36, 57).

tasks.title: Cluster merged findings by location
tasks.acceptance:
tp review --merge and --status gain location_clusters carrying {location, roles, severities, count} for every location reported by more than one role.
The recorded finding count, the clean flag and the --status --check exit code are unchanged (test 28).

tasks.title: Qualify the mechanize recommendation by phase
tasks.acceptance:
next_action's mechanize branch states that a check is worth registering only when the artifact it measures already exists in the review phase.
skills/tp/SKILL.md's mechanize-candidate rule and Workflow D step 3 carry the same qualifier (test 29).

tasks.title: Report a truncated audit as truncated
tasks.acceptance:
tp audit's file_summary gains truncated and total_changed, total_files keeps reporting the audited count, and the notice names both numbers.
The flag is in the payload so --quiet cannot erase it (test 30).

tasks.title: Report per-input merge accounting
tasks.acceptance:
tp review --merge and tp audit --merge report inputs with per-file parsed and skipped counts.
An input with content lines none of which parsed exits 1; a zero-byte or blank-only input exits 0; blank lines never contribute to the condition, and every test pinning the old exit 0 moves with the change (tests 32, 49).
source_sections: ### 8a.4 A dropped role does not merge clean

tasks.title: Exit 2 on an arity violation
tasks.acceptance:
Every command's Args validator exits 2, including cobra's own built-ins, and tp show with no argument names the missing argument.
Every test asserting exit 1 for a wrong argument count moves in this task (test 31).

tasks.title: Fill out the plugin root
tasks.acceptance:
.claude-plugin/plugin.json declares the plugin's identity alongside the existing skills/tp, hooks/ and agents/.
The plugin validates with claude plugin validate and ships no binary (test 24).
tasks.closed_reason:
- .claude-plugin/plugin.json now declares the plugin's identity only (name, version 0.35.0, description, author, homepage, repository, license, keywords) beside the existing marketplace.json; skills/tp and the coming hooks/ and agents/ stay convention-discovered at the plugin root. Verified: the previous manifest failed 'claude plugin validate' outright (inline skills path/triggers objects), the rewritten one passes with and without --strict.
- Version is 0.35.0 because the SessionStart preflight (§6.1) compares 'tp --version' against this field; TestPluginManifestDeclaresIdentity asserts it never falls below that minimum, and that the rejected inline skills block is gone.
- Ships no binary (test 24): TestPluginShipsNoBinary walks the repo and fails on any tracked file starting with an ELF/Mach-O/PE magic, plus asserts .gitignore keeps /tp out. Verified by mutation — a planted 4-byte ELF probe made the test fail with the probe named, and it passes again once removed.
- TestPluginValidatesWithClaudeCLI runs 'claude plugin validate <root> --strict' verbatim and skips when the CLI is absent.
- Quality gate green, each run separately: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0 issues, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0.
Out of scope: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json still pins "skills": ["./skills/tp"] explicitly while plugin.json relies on convention discovery — it validates today, but the redundancy is a drift risk once hooks/ and agents/ land.

tasks.title: Inject orientation on SessionStart
tasks.acceptance:
The SessionStart hook preflights tp's presence and version against plugin.json's, failing with the install command when absent or older.
It then injects tp resume --compact as additional context on every matcher (test 50).

tasks.title: Deny the fenced writes on PreToolUse
tasks.acceptance:
The PreToolUse hook matches Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit and denies .tp-review/ contents, *.tasks.json, .tp/config.json and .tp/local.json.
Shell tools are outside the matcher, so tp's own writes pass (test 25).

tasks.title: Block an incomplete role unit on Stop
tasks.acceptance:
The Stop hook fires only when TP_UNIT_KIND ends in -role, applying the role predicate to the unit's .part and checking for an escalation record.
It blocks a role unit with neither, allows one with either, never fires for a non-role kind, and blocks at most once per unit via stop_hook_active (tests 26, 39, 67).

tasks.title: Bound every shipped hook
tasks.acceptance: Every hook the plugin ships declares a 10-second timeout and exits non-zero rather than hanging (test 43).

tasks.title: Declare the three unit agents
tasks.acceptance:
agents/ declares tp-implementer, tp-reviewer and tp-auditor, with the reviewer and auditor permitted to write only their own findings .part and escalation record and denied every other path.
The claude template appends the documented --agent per unit kind and none for the kinds that take none (tests 44, 55).

tasks.title: Document the unattended run
tasks.acceptance:
README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md carry tp run's command surface, the runner configuration, the unattended restrictions and the plugin's installation and hook behaviour.
CLAUDE.md's reset-native section is rewritten around tp run, with subagent-per-unit as the interactive fallback.
